newsitem.title: CANADA: Heavy rain forecast for Manitoba grainbelt Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rain forecast for Manitoba grainbelt Tuesday.

text.p: Up to four inches of rain were forecast to fall across Manitoba's grainbelt on Tuesday, Environment Canada meteorologist Dale Marciski said.

"We put out a heavy rainfall warning. There should be a few showers and thundershowers tonight with the heaviest rainfall tomorrow between 50 to 100 mm (4 inches) from Brandon to Winnipeg to the Whiteshell (Provincial Park on the Ontario border)," Marciski said.
Spring wheat was in the heading stage across Canada's southern Prairie grainbelt. Manitoba and southeast Saskatchewan were drier than normal to date.
"There will be very little rain elsewhere in the rest of the Prairies except for southeast Saskatchewan," Marciski said.
Estevan and Moose Mountain, Saskatchewan should see 20 mm (0.8 inch) of rain on Tuesday, he said.
Typical yields on Prairie wheat range from 30 to 32 bu/ac but CWB cut them June 11 to 29.5 to 31.5 bu/ac due to dryness.
